newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban planes bomb opposition-held northern city.
newsitem.headline: Taleban planes bomb opposition-held northern city.

text.p: Warplanes of the Islamic Taleban militia launched intensive bombing raids on the opposition-held northern Afghan city of Mazar-i-Sharif on Saturday, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service reported.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said Taleban planes had mounted 60 bombing sorties against Mazar-i-Sharif from airbases in the southern city of Kandahar and from Shindand in Herat province.

It said Taleban planes flying from the big Soviet-built airbase at Bagram north of Kabul had also bombed targets in the Panjsher Valley, stronghold of opposition guerrilla commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
The raids on Mazar-i-Sharif appeared to be retaliation for the heavy defeat suffered by Taleban forces there earlier in the week at the hands of local Shi'ite Moslem and Uzbek fighters.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the bombing, which came three days after a Taleban force of about 3,000 was driven from the city amid heavy casualties.

On Friday, an ethnic Uzbek commander named General Humayun Fauzi warned that any ground or air attack on Mazar-i-Sharif could have "dangerous" consequences for Taleban prisoners in the city, including Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammed Ghous and military commander for the north Mullah Abdul Razzak.
